The 2026 Supply Chain Planning Benchmark Report , based on data from over 2,500 Netstock customers and a survey of more than 150 users at businesses with less than $250m in annual revenue, shows shippers under unceasing strain managing their supply chains. Emerging Chinese carrier CULines is said to have firm plans for an Asia-Middle East service, beginning in late 2026 or early 2027. Hapag-Lloyd last week told customers it would not accept new Upper Gulf bookings to be transhipped via Salalah until further notice. items.title: Why supply and demand no longer tell the whole story in container shipping
items.original_title: Why supply and demand no longer tell the whole story in container shipping
items.summary: For much of container shipping’s history, market conditions could be understood through a relatively straightforward equation. When cargo demand grew faster than available vessel capacity, utilisation and freight rates generally rose. Supply and demand remain at the heart of container shipping, but the equation now contains more variables than it once did. The decline in inventory levels coincided with a period in which North American container imports also softened following the introduction of tariffs in April 2025 and broader uncertainty around consumer demand. Capacity therefore needs to be considered across the full cargo journey, not only in terms of ships and container slots. Geopolitical developments increasingly connect the demand and supply sides of container shipping. Electrification, growing energy demand and investment in digital infrastructure are contributing to growing demand for equipment, components and materials that may move through corridors already carrying substantial volumes of consumer goods. This is another reason supply and demand need to be considered at trade-lane and network level, rather than solely through global totals. Freight rates ultimately reflect the balance between supply and demand.

The RO Code establishes the framework through which flag States assess, authorize and monitor third-party entities that carry out statutory surveys and certification on their behalf. Attention was given to recurrent findings identified through the IMO Member State Audit Scheme (IMSAS), the mandatory mechanism that assesses how effectively Member States implement and enforce IMO instruments. Key findings related to the implementation and enforcement of IMO instruments, oversight programmes, delegation of authority to recognized organizations (ROs), and the evaluation of maritime administration processes. items.summary: Germany has blocked COSCO Shipping’s planned acquisition of an 80% stake in Hamburg freight forwarder Konrad Zippel, overriding an earlier competition clearance on national security grounds. Zippel specialises in container hinterland transport, moving cargo arriving at Hamburg and Bremerhaven onwards by rail, road and inland waterway to industrial centres in eastern Germany and neighbouring markets. German intelligence officials subsequently raised concerns about the deal. Zippel handles between 35% and 90% of container volumes at inland terminals in Berlin, Schkopau and Elsterwerda and also plays a role in logistics supporting Germany’s armed forces. Government officials warned that control of such infrastructure could create dependencies capable of being used as leverage during a political crisis. The decision marks a harder line from Berlin following the long-running controversy over COSCO’s investment in Hamburg’s Container Terminal Tollerort. COSCO originally sought 35% of the terminal operator but was ultimately permitted to take just 24.99% after the German government intervened in 2022 over security concerns. The latest prohibition comes as Germany prepares tougher investment-screening legislation aimed at giving Berlin greater powers to scrutinise acquisitions involving strategic infrastructure and technology.

items.title: Intergr8 Fuels: Global fuel quality remains broadly stable, but localised risks are becoming more important than headline averages
items.original_title: Intergr8 Fuels: Global fuel quality remains broadly stable, but localised risks are becoming more important than headline averages
items.summary: The biannual report, covering fuel quality performance from February to July 2026, finds that global quality averages increasingly mask significant differences between ports, supply chains and fuel characteristics. Changes in crude flows, refinery slates and regional supply pools are contributing to more localised quality exposure. • Localised quality risk: Quality performance varies significantly by port, grade and supply chain, with global averages often masking higher-risk locations and specific quality characteristics. • Biofuel quality: Headline notification rates for biofuel blends remain elevated against conventional ISO reference grades, but much of the apparent exposure is linked to parameters that may not reflect contractual or operational risk. Chris Turner, Technical Manager at Integr8 Fuels: “The headline quality rates tell only part of the story. Risk is increasingly determined by the port, the supply chain and the characteristics of the available fuel pool, rather than by the global average for a grade. Buyers therefore need to look beyond specification and headline price to understand the value and operational implications of the fuel they are actually purchasing.” The report also examines loss control in bunker procurement, showing how energy variance, density differences, additional heating and handling requirements can create costs that remain invisible when fuel is assessed solely against specification limits.

items.title: Port call optimisation pilot projects reveal significant emissions savings potential, new report shows
items.original_title: Port call optimisation pilot projects reveal significant emissions savings potential, new report shows
items.summary: Commercial ships spend between 4% and 6% of their operating year waiting outside ports. That idle time is one of the clearest inefficiencies in shipping, and a combination of slower sailing speeds and port call optimisation can reduce the emissions and fuel currently wasted as ships await an available berth. Instead of sailing fast only to then wait at anchor, port call optimisation allows a ship to arrive when its berth is ready. Cargill Ocean Transportation set out to test the fuel and emissions savings of combining slower sailing speeds with port call optimisation in live commercial operations. With pilot projects at two Australian ports and one in Brazil, the company tested three different mechanisms across 16 voyages and found that the combination can deliver meaningful emissions savings across a range of operational and commercial settings. The findings of the pilots are the subject of a new Global Maritime Forum report, ‘Turning waiting time into savings: Lessons from Cargill’s port call optimisation pilot’. Detailing the pilot projects at the Port of Albany and the Port of Newcastle in Australia, and at Cargill’s grain export terminal in Santarém, Brazil, the report explores the interdependent relationship between port call optimisation and speed reduction.

items.title: IMarEST: From MASS Code to Maritime Practice
items.original_title: IMarEST: From MASS Code to Maritime Practice
items.summary: As shipping becomes increasingly automated, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) has introduced legislation to ensure future technology is safe and secure. But there are significant challenges with taking the new Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) Code from policy to practice. The adoption of the International Maritime Organization’s MASS Code marks an important step in the development of maritime autonomy. Adopted at Marine Safety Committee (MSC) 111, it applied as a non-mandatory code from July 2026, with a mandatory code targeted for 2032. This is a sensible approach as maritime autonomy covers everything from small uncrewed survey vessels to large remotely operated ships, and technology is developing too quickly for a regulation built around particular technical solutions. For each relevant requirement, we should be able to trace a path from the intent of the Code through the functions required to satisfy it, the evidence needed to support the claim, and the organisations or individuals responsible for providing and accepting that evidence. Through the MASS SIG, the Institute has an opportunity to convene the maritime autonomy communities around the practical implementation of the Code and capture lessons as autonomous operations move from controlled trials towards routine use. Timing is also important because the current non-mandatory code provides an opportunity to accumulate operational experience before development of the mandatory code progresses.

Iran attacked roughly two ships for every 100 vessels that crossed the strait in the third quarter, said Michelle Wiese Bockmann, senior maritime intelligence analyst at Windward, which tracks ships for defense departments and governments. Shuttle system In many cases, tankers are bringing crude through Hormuz and then transferring the oil onto ships in the Gulf of Oman that haul it to Asia. Crude oil shipments through Hormuz fluctuate daily, sometimes matching or even exceeding levels before the Iran war, according to data from Kpler, a firm that tracks tankers and global trade flows. Windward estimates crude through Hormuz is averaging 9-10 million bpd compared with a prewar baseline of 14.5 million bpd. items.title: What a 25-Day AIS Blackout Off Libya Tells Us About Mediterranean Narcotics Routes
items.original_title: What a 25-Day AIS Blackout Off Libya Tells Us About Mediterranean Narcotics Routes
items.summary: The 25-Day Gap Between Albania and Libya In late August 2026, a Mali-flagged general cargo vessel left an Albanian port, declared Egypt as its destination, and switched off its AIS transponder in open water off eastern Libya. For 25 days and 8 hours, nothing was transmitted. When it reappeared on September 23, it was at nearly the same position where it had gone dark. What happened off Libya in late August was consistent with a pattern the vessel had been establishing for months. What One Voyage Says About Mediterranean Narcotics Routes What makes this case worth attention is not the single dark activity, but the repeatability built into it. A vessel that returns consistently to the same Albanian base, under a flag with no oversight behind it, with a documented history of going dark off the same coasts, is a vessel whose operational pattern can be run again. The March 2026 Sinai gaps and the August–September Libya gap are consistent with a methodology, not an improvisation. For interdiction and compliance stakeholders tracking Mediterranean narcotics routes, the question is not whether this specific voyage carried something. The vessel that vanished for 25 days off Libya may be one example of a wider operational practice.

items.summary: A 22-year-old product tanker sanctioned by the European Union is making an unusual late-season voyage along Russia’s Northern Sea Route, highlighting the growing use of older, lower-specification vessels to move petroleum products through the Arctic. The Dakar , a 21,300-dwt oil and chemical products tanker built in 2004, is carrying methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE), a gasoline additive, and appears to be heading west along Russia’s Arctic coast, according vessel tracking data. The cargo was loaded onto another vessel in China in August before being transferred to Dakar off Yeosu, South Korea, in September. That distinguishes it from non-ice-class tankers, while placing it well below the Arc4 and higher ice-class vessels purpose-built for regular Arctic operations. A similar voyage last year demonstrated the risk: the non-ice-class Suezmax Lynx was forced to wait for several day s after encountering sea ice near 72 degrees north while carrying Russian crude toward China. Dakar ’s voyage also follows a sharp increase in Russian oil exports to Asia through the Arctic this year. Reuters reported in August that seven tankers had already moved roughly 6 million barrels of crude through the NSR, nearly half the total shipped by tankers through the route during all of 2025.

items.original_title: SFL – Sale of four LR2 and three Suezmax tankers, and termination of charters
items.summary: SFL Corporation Ltd. announced that it has agreed to sell four 2014- and 2015-built LR2 product tankers and three 2019-built Suezmax tankers, currently on time charters to Trafigura, a global leader in the commodities industry. The vessels were acquired in 2021 and 2022, and the charter agreements include a profit share mechanism in the event of a profitable sale. The Company has now agreed to sell the vessels to Trafigura with delivery in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, and the existing charters will terminate when the vessels are delivered to the buyer. The sales price per vessel is confidential, but after profit share and repayment of associated debt, the net cash proceeds to SFL is estimated at approximately $275 million in aggregate. The Company currently estimates an aggregate book gain of approximately $175 million from the transaction. Hjertaker, Chief Executive Officer of SFL Management AS, commented: “This transaction demonstrates the intrinsic value of our operating platform. We have enjoyed strong cash flows from the vessels over the last five years, and in addition retained a significant share of the asset value upside, which is crystallizing now. We expect to reinvest the proceeds in new accretive investments that will build our long-term distribution capacity.” Source: Ship Finance International

The revised agreements extend the Bakken contracts and are expected to reduce Chevron’s Bakken unit midstream costs by approximately 50%, enhancing future earnings and return on capital employed. In exchange for the improved long-term commercial framework and $200 million in cash consideration, Chevron will transfer to Hess Midstream its ownership interests and general partner position in Hess Midstream, as well as its DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets. Chevron expects this transaction to be accretive to return on capital employed by 0.5% on an absolute basis and generate long-term future economic value through a lower cost structure and improved earnings. At closing, Chevron expects to recognize a one-time after-tax loss estimated at approximately $3 to $4 billion,1 given that the company is unable to recognize future Bakken midstream cost savings as an asset. “This transaction resets the commercial framework between our upstream and midstream assets in the Bakken and DJ Basins,” said Andy Walz, Chevron’s President of Downstream, Midstream and Chemicals.

items.summary: Trafigura Group bought seven oil tankers from New York-listed SFL Corp., in the latest example of how trading houses and state energy companies are acquiring vessels to ship crude and products. Disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have drawn in scores of tankers to shuttle key oil flows out to the global market, while growing risks in the Red Sea are leading to longer voyage routes and times. That’s prompted a rush to snap up tankers as rates to charter vessels soar. Trafigura bought four oil product tankers known as LR2s — built in 2014 and 2015 — and three suezmax tankers built in 2019, SFL said in a statement on Wednesday. SFL said it had made an “aggregate book gain” of $175 million from the deal, without disclosing the sale price of the vessels. Strong demand for prompt availability of oil carriers have pushed the resale values of tankers higher. A 10-year-old Aframax, which is the same size as an LR2 tanker, was assessed to be worth $72.5 million last week, while a Suezmax of the same age could sell for $110 million, Clarkson data show. Trafigura recently made its first foray into launching a public company, listing a supertanker vehicle Volare Shipping Ltd.

items.title: Bad weather creates headwinds for trade between the Americas
items.original_title: Bad weather creates headwinds for trade between the Americas
items.summary: The easing of restrictions on Panama Canal transits has brought some relief to exporters in South America, but other headwinds remain, which could accelerate the widening gap between imports and exports. This month, Seaboard Marine is expanding its West Coast South America service to the US East Coast with a call at Gloucester City. The first arrival at the New Jersey port is scheduled for 25 October. The gap widened 20%, to 1.7m teu. Likewise, CTS data show South America’s maritime exports to North America shrank 1.1% year on year in July, whereas volume in the opposite direction expanded 7.2%. On a positive note, the Global Liner Performance Report for September, by Sea-Intelligence, shows schedule reliability between South and North America improved in both directions in the July/August period. items.summary: Seven major ports across Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany have secured government backing for a wider cross-border programme aimed at cutting regulatory barriers and accelerating automated freight and energy infrastructure across the Antwerp-Rotterdam-Rhine-Ruhr corridor. The agreement was reached at a Port Summit in Meise this week between the governments of Flanders, the Netherlands and North Rhine-Westphalia and the port authorities of Duisport, North Sea Port, Antwerp-Bruges, Cologne/HGK, Moerdijk, Oostende and Rotterdam. One of the more concrete logistics measures is a plan to use cross-border corridors such as Antwerp-Rotterdam for automated freight transport by road and inland waterway. The three governments also want closer cooperation on drones, with rules and procedures to be aligned across borders. The wider programme covers a common market for secondary raw materials, coordinated development of hydrogen and CO2 transport infrastructure and joint work on inland navigation and strategic water management. Ports in the region have also been pushing for so-called acceleration areas to shorten planning and permitting times for major infrastructure and industrial projects. That call has now been incorporated into the summit declaration, alongside moves to reduce regulatory differences between the three jurisdictions. The three governments will take the programme to Brussels, asking the European Commission to recognise the Antwerp-Rotterdam-Rhine-Ruhr Area, or ARRRA, as a strategic European port-industrial cluster.

Prices initially went vertical after US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 and the subsequent disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Ship & Bunker data shows Singapore VLSFO rising from $521.50 per tonne immediately before the conflict to a peak of $1,120.50 by March 13. The market subsequently retreated as supply chains adjusted and hopes periodically surfaced of a diplomatic breakthrough, but bunker prices have never returned close to their pre-war levels, and have been increasing again in recent weeks. In Singapore, the absolute discount enjoyed by scrubber-fitted ships burning HSFO has widened from around $77 per tonne immediately before the war to roughly $122 today, even though the price of HSFO itself has surged.

The crude transfers totaled an estimated 9 million barrels and were ultimately destined for Chinese independent refiners, commonly known as “teapots.” The activity has continued despite growing scrutiny of the large network of sanctioned and Iran-linked vessels operating in the region. The depletion of offshore storage comes even as oil exports from other Persian Gulf producers have recovered. If UANI’s estimate of roughly 10 million barrels remaining in Malaysian floating storage is accurate, the pool of crude available outside the blockade has fallen sharply. With no new crude reaching those offshore inventories, continued deliveries to China would increasingly depend on drawing down a finite stockpile rather than replacing exported barrels.

items.summary: File Photo: Oil tanker Al Shaffiah sails at the sea near the Omani coast, as seen from Musandam, Oman, June 26, 2026. The blockade has all but choked off Iranian exports, while other Gulf producers have adapted to attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping by relying on so-called dark transits — switching off tankers’ tracking systems to evade detection — to protect the oil flows that underpin their economies. Flows of crude, condensate and refined fuels including LPG averaged 19.2 million barrels per day (bpd) from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Iraq and the UAE, Vortexa data showed, compared with an average of about 23.6 million bpd in the year that preceded the outbreak of the Iran war on February 28. items.title: Panama Canal Expands Advance Transit Reservations for 2027 Dry Season
items.original_title: Panama Canal Expands Advance Transit Reservations for 2027 Dry Season
items.summary: The Panama Canal is expanding its long-term transit reservation program to the Panamax locks for the first time, giving more shipping customers the ability to secure passage months in advance during the 2027 dry season. The Panama Canal Authority said Monday that the next phase of its Long-term Slot Allocation, or LoTSA, program will cover transits from January 3 through April 3, 2027. The program will continue at the Neopanamax locks while a new pilot program introduces long-term slot allocations for vessels using the Panamax locks. The expansion comes as the Panama Canal continues adjusting its operating model following the severe drought that sharply restricted daily transits in 2023 and 2024 and exposed the vulnerability of the freshwater-dependent waterway to changing rainfall conditions. For carriers and vessel operators, the attraction of LoTSA is straightforward: guaranteed access to scarce transit capacity can make voyage planning more reliable, particularly during the dry season when water availability has historically placed the greatest pressure on Canal operations. By extending the program to the Panamax locks, the Canal is making that option available to a broader portion of the commercial fleet for the first time. The Panama Canal is easing restrictions on vessel draft and daily transits after improved rainfall and water-saving measures helped stabilize conditions in the waterway’s drought-sensitive watershed.

items.summary: China’s exclusion of soybeans from its planned tariff-reduction framework has left exporters optimistic that Beijing will increase purchases of other US farm and food products in the coming months to fulfill a commitment made earlier this year. China’s Ministry of Commerce said Sept. 28 that Beijing would consider reducing tariffs on a range of US agricultural and animal-protein products, including beef, pork, corn and wheat, but excluded soybeans. China purchased more than $10 billion in US farm and food products from January through July 2026, including $4.9 billion of soybeans and $5.2 billion of other agricultural commodities, according to US Census Bureau trade data. “Removal of the remaining 10% tariff that China has on US agricultural commodities could be key to boosting US competitiveness in the Chinese market,” S&P Global Energy CERA analysts said in a Sept. US beef and pork exports have historically accounted for a significant share of China’s purchases of US agricultural and food products, US traders said. During the tariff dispute in early 2025, China reduced its purchases of US pork and suspended US beef imports after Beijing stopped renewing export licenses for US meat-processing facilities in March 2025. China imposes a 13% duty on US soybeans, comprising a 3% most-favored-nation tariff and an additional 10% levy.

items.title: Korea pushes SMR ship lead as outdated rules spur global standards race
items.original_title: Korea pushes SMR ship lead as outdated rules spur global standards race
items.summary: As Korea’s shipbuilding industry accelerates development of vessels equipped with small modular reactors (SMRs), calls are growing for the creation of international rules. Existing nuclear safety regulations focus on land-based nuclear power plants, and maritime regulations focus on conventional ships, leaving a gap for “ships carrying reactors,” where standards to apply are not fully established. With the offshore SMR market preparing for commercial use, leading the formation of international standards and rules—no less than technology development—is seen as a factor that will determine future market competitiveness. For ships carrying next-generation SMRs to call at ports around the world, standards are needed that cover not only reactor safety but also maritime accidents such as collisions and groundings, port entry, and emergency response. International liability rules for damages in the event of an accident involving a nuclear-powered ship are also not functioning properly. IMO and International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) standards on port entry conditions were last revised in 1968. The Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute (KAERI) and Samsung Heavy Industries are developing a 174,000-cubic-meter LNG carrier based on a marine MSR, and HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering has designed a nuclear-powered container ship equipped with an SMR, winning approval in principle from DNV in Oct.

items.title: Europe’s diesel tightness persists into Q4
items.original_title: Europe’s diesel tightness persists into Q4
items.summary: Europe’s diesel/gasoil imports from outside the region hit the lowest September on record. Diesel/gasoil exports pointed to Europe from outside regions averaged only 1mbd in September, down 600kbd y-o-y. Russia and the Middle East account for most of the drop, together down 580kbd compared to last year. Diesel on the water pointed to Europe is more than 25% below last year’s levels, all points indicating that October will be another month of weak arrivals. Europe’s implied refinery runs fell by around 600kbd in September (according to our estimates), after reaching a year-to-date high in August. Strong margins have delayed maintenance at key refineries into 2027, including Tarragona (180kbd), Thessaloniki (66kbd) and Gonfreville (247kbd) (Argus), so maintenance season is likely to already have peaked in September this year, as opposed to the usual October. The US is still the key external supplier The US supplied 41% of Europe’s external diesel in September, at 400kbd, above year-ago levels but down from a dataset high of 445kbd in August. A growing portion of China’s diesel cargoes are moving on LR2s. Unless Asia’s diesel arb to Europe widens, China’s Q4 barrels will likely keep prioritising shorter-haul destinations amid high freight costs.

items.summary: Italian product tanker owner d’Amico International Shipping has exercised a $14m purchase option on the 2014-built MR tanker High Fidelity , paving the way for its entire operating fleet to return to full ownership. The ship is one of the last two vessels in d’Amico’s fleet still operating under bareboat arrangements. The company currently controls 28 product tankers on the water — 16 MRs, six handysizes and six LR1s — comprising 26 owned ships and two bareboat-chartered units. Once both transfers are completed, d’Amico will have no remaining bareboat-chartered ships. Both vessels were refinanced through sale-and-leaseback structures in 2022. At the time, d’Amico exercised previous options on High Discovery and High Fidelity for $20.3m and $19.2m respectively before refinancing them under new 10-year bareboat leases containing fresh purchase options. items.original_title: HD Hyundai delivers world’s first lashing-free containership
items.summary: HD Hyundai has delivered what it says is the world’s first containership designed to eliminate manual lashing, removing one of the most labour-intensive jobs in container shipping. The 13,000 teu vessel, which is methanol dual-fuelled, has been handed over toFrance’s CMA CGM after being built using HD Hyundai’s proprietary hybrid lashing-free system. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries developed and verified the core technology, while HD Hyundai Samho carried out detailed design and construction. HD Hyundai’s new arrangement does away with that work by extending cell guides above deck, allowing containers to be held in place without traditional lashing. The breakthrough centres on what HD Hyundai calls a portable bench, a standardised structure fitted between cell guides. The unit is the same size as a 40 ft container, meaning terminal cranes can handle it as part of normal cargo operations. HD Hyundai says the design boosts deck cargo capacity by more than 10% compared with similar existing ships while improving operational stability in heavy weather. The technology was presented to the IMO’s Sub-Committee on Carriage of Cargoes and Containers in 2024 and has since secured multiple patents. The Korean yard plans to expand the lashing-free technology to small and mid-sized vessels soon.

items.original_title: Black Sea merchant shipping comes under fresh drone attack
items.summary: Commercial shipping in the western Black Sea has come under a fresh wave of attacks, with another general cargoship sinking and a second catching fire off Bulgaria barely a day after the loss of the Royad Mammadov off Romania. According to UK maritime security specialist Vanguard Tech, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan and Palau-flagged Able issued distress signals around 70–80 nautical miles east of Byala and Cape St Atanas, inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. Bulgarian sources state that both vessels had been struck by drones. The Turkish-owned, St Kitts and Nevis-flagged vessel was carrying corn from Izmail to Italy when it caught fire and sank around 30 nautical miles south of Sfantu Gheorghe. Two seafarers were killed and 11 rescued. But there are enough signs beneath the surface to start asking a more awkward question: how much of this cycle is left, and which sectors are closest to finding out?
